submitter: bugfix-222 lane (fabrication gate declaration tier convicts the denial) — round 1, submitted alongside the commit per the 2026-07-30 trailer rule
rationale: bugs_open/222, filed 2026-08-08 by the mortgagecalculator adoption lane and reproduced live the same day: the fabrication gate's Tier A declaration check (check_tool_fabrication_action.go, three regexes matching a synthetic/fabrication qualifier within 48-64 chars of a data noun) has no negation awareness, so the comment '// In-memory portfolio store (no fabricated data — starts empty)' — a DENIAL, on a tool that genuinely starts empty and holds only user-entered records — was convicted as a declaration of fabrication. The recreate prompt's own Data Integrity section spends ~9 lines forbidding fabrication, so a conscientious model echoing that prohibition as a comment is the common case, not a freak one (the same class 016b already documents for this bug). A correct, paid-for recreation was discarded to needs_human_review; the same page was convicted once before (signals purged, unread). THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING THAT SHAPED THIS FIX: this platform already has a negation guard for exactly this false-positive class — negatedClaimMatch in platform/orchestration/datahelpers/claims.go, registered as CLM-017, shared by two consumers (ScanBannedClaims, ScanAttributedUncitedStats) under an explicit CLM-004 anti-drift doctrine ('one matching rule here, not two that diverge'). Naive reuse does not fix the bug: negationCueRe DELIBERATELY excludes bare 'no' and 'without' (they are intensifiers in marketing prose — 'Without exception, every claim is verified' — and the exclusion is pinned by TestBareNoIsAKnownResidualOfTheSharedGuard), and the motivating payload is negated by exactly the cue the claims layer excludes. Widening the shared cue regex to fix an unrelated gate would risk reintroducing the false negative CLM-017 exists to prevent, in a layer that runs at BLOCKER severity on live marketing copy. So this plan extracts the ALGORITHM (bounded backwards window, clause-boundary trim, cue test — including a non-obvious multibyte-rune fix already paid for) as an exported, parameterised NegationGuard, and gives the fabrication gate its OWN vocabulary (includes no/without/zero/instead of/rather than — each justified against a counter-example of a REAL declaration it must not license) over the SAME algorithm. negatedClaimMatch becomes a one-line wrapper; the full datahelpers suite — including the pinned bare-no residual test — passes with ZERO test-file edits, which is the mechanical proof the claims layer's guarantee is unchanged. A SECOND subtlety, already recorded in this codebase for a different consumer (CLM-019, claims_attributed.go): a cue-spanning match can put the negation INSIDE the matched span, invisible to a scan from the match's overall start. Two of the fabrication gate's three Tier-A regexes put the qualifier SECOND (data noun first), so this recurs here — solved with a declPattern{re, qualGroup} pairing over FindAllStringSubmatchIndex, scanning from the qualifier's own submatch position regardless of which group it lands in (one regex, fabGenerateVerbData, needed its previously-unparenthesised verb wrapped as a capture group; nothing else read that group). PLAN DRAFTED WITH A SEPARATE MODEL PASS (fable) specifically to catch reuse-vs-reinvent mistakes before code was written — and it did: my own research notes had wrongly claimed 'no existing negation-aware helper', caught before implementation, logged to WRONG_CALLS.md. TESTED: reproduction-first (five new test functions written and run RED against unfixed code before any fix landed, confirming every fixture actually reproduces — two fixture-authoring mistakes of my own were caught this way, not by reading the regex), then a full mutation-and-control triple against a clean git archive HEAD overlay (the shared tree carries unrelated dirty files from other sessions in the same packages): killing the guard fails exactly the tests that should depend on it; forcing it to always-negate fails the tests asserting a real declaration must survive, while the untouched synthetic-PII arm stayed convicted through that same mutation — evidence, not argument, that Tier B/the PII arm remain a backstop against a defensively-phrased real fabrication (the residual risk this fix accepts). An unrelated control mutation (an adjacent Tier B threshold) left every new test green, so none are vacuously sensitive. NOT ARCHITECTURE-SCOPE under the 2026-07-29 ruling: this adds an opt-in exported helper reachable by nothing until a caller names it, and changes no shared mechanism's GUARANTEE — the claims layer's cue regex, window, boundary and both consumers are byte-for-byte untouched (mechanically proven, not asserted). The one behaviour that changes is the fabrication gate's own false-positive rate, in the reduction direction only: every failure mode still routes to needs_human_review, never to deploying a fabrication, and a forward-positioned denial ('Mock data is not used') is a deliberately pinned, documented residual (same shape as CLM-017's own bare-no residual), not a silent gap. Consumers named and told: the claims layer (no guarantee change — T-0 proof) and mortgagecalculator_couk_adoption (bugs_open/222's filing lane, whose prompt-side comment-style workaround this retires once live). Concept-register entry (CLM-020) ships in the same commit.

plan.summary: bugs_open/222: extract CLM-017's negation-guard algorithm from datahelpers/claims.go as an exported, parameterised NegationGuard (claims vocabulary and both existing consumers untouched), and apply it in the fabrication gate's Tier A declaration check with a domain-tuned cue vocabulary, scanned from each match's qualifier submatch position so a negator cannot hide inside a regex span (the CLM-019 lesson, generalised past one fixed offset).

edits.rationale: Extracts the existing negatedClaimMatch algorithm into an exported, parameterised primitive so a second domain (the fabrication gate) can reuse the scanning mechanics without reimplementing them or reaching into this package's cue vocabulary. negatedClaimMatch becomes a one-line wrapper with an IDENTICAL body — zero behaviour change for CLM-017's two live consumers, proven by the full datahelpers suite passing with no test file touched.

Mechanical proof the extraction is domain-parametric AND that claimNegationGuard's own vocabulary was not widened to make it so: a guard built with a DIFFERENT cue regex (including bare 'no', which negationCueRe deliberately excludes) suppresses at a position claimNegationGuard does not, over the identical string.

The fabrication-domain fix. A cue vocabulary that DOES include no/without/zero (each justified against a real-declaration counter-example it must not license), bound to datahelpers.NegationGuard with a 32-byte window and a bracket-inclusive clause boundary (code comments are terse; brackets end a clause in JS/HTML that prose punctuation would not). declPattern pairs each Tier-A regex with its qualifier's submatch index so the guard is asked about the qualifier's OWN position, not the match start — the CLM-019 lesson, since fabDataNearQualifier and fabGenerateVerbData put the qualifier SECOND and a negator between the two groups lands inside the match. fabGenerateVerbData's verb is wrapped as a capture group for this reason; nothing else read that group. Suppressed matches are surfaced in Signals (never counted toward Fabricated) so a guard that starts eating real findings is observable, mirroring ScanBannedClaimsIgnoringNegation's argument in claims.go. The synthetic-PII arm is deliberately NOT guarded: an identifier generator is code the recreation runs, not deniable prose.

Written and run RED against unfixed code before any fix landed (confirmed each fixture genuinely reproduces — two of my own fixture-authoring mistakes were caught this way: one fixture matched no regex at all, one matched an unrelated SECOND coincidental hit). T-1 is the bug's exact payload. T-2 is the required non-vacuity/positional proof (a real declaration survives an unrelated negation elsewhere in the document). T-3 pins the CLM-019 inside-the-span lesson for both affected regexes. T-4 sweeps the cue vocabulary, one row per cue. T-7 pins the deliberate forward-negation residual, in the same style as TestBareNoIsAKnownResidualOfTheSharedGuard.

Seam registration in the same commit that ships it, per the platform-seams convention: a new exported, reusable mechanism (NegationGuard) another workstream could call, cross-linked from CLM-017 (the algorithm/vocabulary it exports without touching) and CLM-019 (the inside-the-span lesson it generalises past a single fixed offset).
